```{r setup, include=FALSE}

source("R/intermediate_pipeline.R")
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr)
seaweed <- cp_seaweed()
seaweed$zone <- factor(seaweed$zone, levels = c("North", "Centre", "South"))
wq <- cp_wq_clean()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2, out.width = "90%")
```

::: objectives
::: en
#### By the end of this session you will be able to
- show **means with error bars** (SD, SE or 95 % CI) for groups side by side (`position_dodge`);
- draw **time series** with readable date axes;
- **order** categories by their values and **annotate** a graph (lines, text, areas);
- write your own **theme function** (Session I6) and produce **one figure per group** with a loop (Session I5);
- combine several graphs in one figure with **patchwork** and export it for a report.
:::
::: fr
#### À la fin de cette séance vous saurez
- montrer des **moyennes avec barres d'erreur** (ET, ES ou IC à 95 %) pour des groupes côte à côte (`position_dodge`) ;
- tracer des **séries temporelles** avec des axes de dates lisibles ;
- **ordonner** des catégories selon leurs valeurs et **annoter** un graphique (lignes, texte, zones) ;
- écrire votre propre **fonction de thème** (séance I6) et produire **une figure par groupe** avec une boucle (séance I5) ;
- combiner plusieurs graphiques en une figure avec **patchwork** et l'exporter pour un rapport.
:::
:::

`r dl("I3_seaweed_analysis.csv", "checkpoint: I3_seaweed_analysis.csv", dir = "data/checkpoints")` `r dl("I2_water_quality_clean.csv", "checkpoint: I2_water_quality_clean.csv", dir = "data/checkpoints")`

## [Means and error bars]{.en}[Moyennes et barres d'erreur]{.fr} {#errorbars}

::: en
First compute the summary per group (Session I6 functions are handy), then draw it. The **95 % confidence interval** of a mean is approximately mean ± 1.96 × SE (for large samples): it shows the precision of the mean, and is the most informative choice when comparing groups. Always say in the caption which one you show.
:::
::: fr
Calculez d'abord le résumé par groupe (les fonctions de la séance I6 sont pratiques), puis tracez-le. L'**intervalle de confiance à 95 %** d'une moyenne vaut environ moyenne ± 1,96 × ES (pour les grands échantillons) : il montre la précision de la moyenne, et c'est le choix le plus informatif pour comparer des groupes. Indiquez toujours dans la légende lequel vous montrez.
:::

```{r}
se <- function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
summ <- seaweed %>%
  group_by(zone, technique) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(sgr)), mean = mean(sgr, na.rm = TRUE), se = se(sgr), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(low = mean - 1.96 * se, high = mean + 1.96 * se)
summ
```

```{r}
dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.5)          # shift the two techniques side by side
ggplot(summ, aes(zone, mean, colour = technique)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), position = dodge, size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("long-line" = "#1b7f8c", "off-bottom" = "#d9694a")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean SGR (% per day)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Points: means; bars: 95 % confidence intervals") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

::: en
For bars, use `geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8))` + `geom_errorbar(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.2)` — the dodge width must be the **same** in both layers. Points (`geom_pointrange`) are often better than bars: bars suggest that values start at zero, which is not meaningful for a rate or a temperature.
:::
::: fr
Pour des barres, utilisez `geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8))` + `geom_errorbar(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.2)` — la largeur de décalage doit être la **même** dans les deux couches. Les points (`geom_pointrange`) sont souvent préférables aux barres : les barres suggèrent que les valeurs partent de zéro, ce qui n'a pas de sens pour un taux ou une température.
:::

## [Time series]{.en}[Séries temporelles]{.fr} {#time}

::: en
With a `Date` column on the x-axis, `scale_x_date()` controls the ticks: `date_breaks = "3 months"`, `date_labels = "%b %Y"` (format codes of Session I1). `geom_line()` joins the points **of the same group**: set `group` or `colour`.
:::
::: fr
Avec une colonne `Date` sur l'axe x, `scale_x_date()` contrôle les graduations : `date_breaks = "3 months"`, `date_labels = "%b %Y"` (codes de format de la séance I1). `geom_line()` relie les points **d'un même groupe** : précisez `group` ou `colour`.
:::

```{r}
st <- read.csv("data/stations.csv")
wq_zone <- wq %>% left_join(st[, c("station", "zone")], by = "station") %>%
  group_by(zone, date) %>% summarise(temp = mean(temp_C, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(wq_zone, aes(date, temp, colour = zone)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean temperature (°C)", colour = "Zone") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## [Ordering and annotating]{.en}[Ordonner et annoter]{.fr} {#annotate}

::: en
`reorder(category, value, FUN = median)` sorts categories by a summary of the values — a ranked graph is much faster to read. Annotations guide the reader: a reference line (`geom_hline()`), a shaded period (`annotate("rect")`), a text label (`annotate("text")`).
:::
::: fr
`reorder(catégorie, valeur, FUN = median)` trie les catégories selon un résumé des valeurs — un graphique classé se lit beaucoup plus vite. Les annotations guident le lecteur : une ligne de référence (`geom_hline()`), une période ombrée (`annotate("rect")`), un texte (`annotate("text")`).
:::

```{r}
overall <- mean(seaweed$sgr, na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(seaweed, aes(reorder(village, sgr, FUN = median, na.rm = TRUE), sgr)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#a8d5da", na.rm = TRUE, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = overall, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d9694a") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = overall + 0.15, label = "cooperative mean", colour = "#d9694a", size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SGR (% per day)") + theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot(wq_zone, aes(date, temp, colour = zone)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = as.Date("2024-11-01"), xmax = as.Date("2025-04-30"),
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.15, fill = "#1b7f8c") +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2025-01-31"), y = 23.3, label = "wet season", colour = "#0b3d5c") +
  geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs(x = NULL, y = "°C")
```

## [Your own theme, and one figure per group]{.en}[Votre propre thème, et une figure par groupe]{.fr} {#own-theme}

::: en
A **function returning a theme** (Session I6) gives all your report figures the same look, and you change it in one place. A **loop** (Session I5) saves one figure per village.
:::
::: fr
Une **fonction qui renvoie un thème** (séance I6) donne le même aspect à toutes les figures d'un rapport, et on la modifie à un seul endroit. Une **boucle** (séance I5) enregistre une figure par village.
:::

```{r}
theme_coop <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#0b3d5c"),
          legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
p_v <- function(v) {
  d <- seaweed[seaweed$village == v, ]
  ggplot(d, aes(planting_date, sgr, colour = technique)) +
    geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
    labs(title = v, x = NULL, y = "SGR (% per day)") + theme_coop()
}
p_v("Lovobe")
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
dir.create("outputs/figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
for (v in unique(seaweed$village)) {
  ggsave(file.path("outputs/figures", paste0("sgr_", v, ".png")), p_v(v),
         width = 16, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
}
```

## [Combining graphs with patchwork]{.en}[Combiner des graphiques avec patchwork]{.fr} {#patchwork}

::: en
**patchwork** adds graphs together: `p1 + p2` side by side, `p1 / p2` stacked, `(p1 | p2) / p3` mixed. `plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")` adds the letters A, B, C used in articles.
:::
::: fr
**patchwork** additionne des graphiques : `p1 + p2` côte à côte, `p1 / p2` empilés, `(p1 | p2) / p3` combinés. `plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")` ajoute les lettres A, B, C utilisées dans les articles.
:::

```{r, fig.height=6.5, message=FALSE}
library(patchwork)
pA <- ggplot(wq_zone, aes(date, temp, colour = zone)) + geom_line() + theme_coop() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Temperature (°C)", colour = NULL)
pB <- ggplot(summ, aes(zone, mean, colour = technique)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), position = dodge) + theme_coop() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SGR (% per day)", colour = NULL)
pC <- ggplot(seaweed, aes(temp_mean, sgr)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, na.rm = TRUE, colour = "#d9694a") + theme_coop() +
  labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "SGR (% per day)")
(pA) / (pB | pC) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A",
                                    title = "Sea temperature and seaweed growth, 2024–2025")
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fig <- (pA) / (pB | pC) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
ggsave("outputs/figure_1.png", fig, width = 18, height = 16, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
ggsave("outputs/figure_1.pdf", fig, width = 18, height = 16, units = "cm")   # vector, for printing
```

::: {.callout .ecology}
::: en
Panel C already suggests the answer to one of the cooperative's questions: growth is **not** a straight line of temperature — it is best around 25–26 °C and drops when the water is warmer. Keep this in mind for the correlation in Session I10.
:::
::: fr
Le panneau C suggère déjà la réponse à une question de la coopérative : la croissance n'est **pas** une droite de la température — elle est meilleure autour de 25–26 °C et baisse quand l'eau est plus chaude. Gardez-le en tête pour la corrélation de la séance I10.
:::
:::

## [Application work & quiz]{.en}[Travail d'application et quiz]{.fr} {#application}

```{r answers, include=FALSE}
S <- cp_seaweed()
sm <- S %>% group_by(zone, technique) %>% summarise(m = mean(sgr, na.rm = TRUE), s = se(sgr), .groups = "drop")
r <- sm[sm$zone == "North" & sm$technique == "off-bottom", ]
a1 <- round(r$m + 1.96 * r$s, 3)
st <- read.csv("data/stations.csv")
wz <- cp_wq_clean() %>% left_join(st[, c("station", "zone")], by = "station") %>%
  group_by(zone, date) %>% summarise(temp = mean(temp_C, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
a2 <- as.character(wz$date[which.max(wz$temp)])
a3 <- round(max(wz$temp), 2)
med <- tapply(S$sgr, S$village, median, na.rm = TRUE); a4 <- names(which.max(med)); a5 <- names(which.min(med))
sy <- S %>% group_by(season, year) %>% summarise(m = mean(sgr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
a6 <- round(sy$m[sy$season == "wet" & sy$year == 2025], 3)
```

::: application
::: en
### Application work I8

Script `scripts/i08_ggplot.R`, using your `theme_coop()`.

1. Plot mean SGR ± 95 % CI by zone and technique (`geom_pointrange`, dodge). Upper limit of the CI for **off-bottom** lines in the **North** (3 decimals)?
2. Time series of mean temperature per zone. On which date (`yyyy-mm-dd`) is the highest mean recorded, and what is its value (2 decimals)?
3. Boxplots of SGR by village ordered by median. Which village has the **highest** median? The **lowest**?
4. Mean SGR per season and year (`group_by(season, year)`), shown as points joined by lines. Value for the **wet season 2025** (3 decimals)?
5. Combine three of your graphs with patchwork (tags A, B, C) and save the figure in PNG and PDF.
6. Use a loop to save one SGR figure per village.
:::
::: fr
### Travail d'application I8

Script `scripts/i08_ggplot.R`, avec votre `theme_coop()`.

1. Tracez le SGR moyen ± IC à 95 % par zone et technique (`geom_pointrange`, décalage). Borne supérieure de l'IC des lignes **off-bottom** du **Nord** (3 décimales) ?
2. Série temporelle de la température moyenne par zone. À quelle date (`aaaa-mm-jj`) la moyenne la plus élevée est-elle enregistrée ? Donnez la date, et la valeur (2 décimales).
3. Boxplots du SGR par village ordonnés par médiane. Quel village a la médiane la **plus élevée** ? La **plus faible** ?
4. SGR moyen par saison et par année (`group_by(season, year)`), en points reliés par des lignes. Valeur pour la **saison des pluies 2025** (3 décimales) ?
5. Combinez trois de vos graphiques avec patchwork (étiquettes A, B, C) et enregistrez la figure en PNG et en PDF.
6. Avec une boucle, enregistrez une figure de SGR par village.
:::
:::

::: hint
::: en
Question 2: after building `wq_zone`, `wq_zone[which.max(wq_zone$temp), ]` gives the row of the maximum.
:::
::: fr
Question 2 : après avoir construit `wq_zone`, `wq_zone[which.max(wq_zone$temp), ]` donne la ligne du maximum.
:::
:::

```{r quiz, echo=FALSE}
quiz("i08", list(
  q_num("1. Upper 95 % CI limit, off-bottom, North (3 decimals)?", "1. Borne supérieure de l'IC 95 %, off-bottom, Nord (3 décimales) ?", a1, tol = 0.0006),
  q_text("2a. Date of the highest mean temperature (yyyy-mm-dd)?", "2a. Date de la température moyenne la plus élevée (aaaa-mm-jj) ?", a2),
  q_num("2b. Its value (2 decimals)?", "2b. Sa valeur (2 décimales) ?", a3, tol = 0.006),
  q_text("3a. Village with the highest median SGR?", "3a. Village au SGR médian le plus élevé ?", a4),
  q_text("3b. Village with the lowest median SGR?", "3b. Village au SGR médian le plus faible ?", a5),
  q_num("4. Mean SGR, wet season 2025 (3 decimals)?", "4. SGR moyen, saison des pluies 2025 (3 décimales) ?", a6, tol = 0.0006),
  q_mcq("5. In patchwork, (p1 | p2) / p3 gives:", "5. Avec patchwork, (p1 | p2) / p3 donne :",
        c("three plots in a row", "p1 and p2 side by side, p3 below", "p3 above p1 and p2", "an error"),
        c("trois graphiques en ligne", "p1 et p2 côte à côte, p3 en dessous", "p3 au-dessus de p1 et p2", "une erreur"), correct = 2),
  q_mcq("6. Why must position_dodge() have the same width in geom_col() and geom_errorbar()?", "6. Pourquoi position_dodge() doit-il avoir la même largeur dans geom_col() et geom_errorbar() ?",
        c("Otherwise the error bars are not centred on their bars", "To save memory", "It does not matter", "Because of the colours"),
        c("Sinon les barres d'erreur ne sont pas centrées sur leurs barres", "Pour économiser la mémoire", "Cela n'a pas d'importance", "À cause des couleurs"), correct = 1)
))
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="i08"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(patchwork)
seaweed <- read.csv("data/checkpoints/I3_seaweed_analysis.csv")
seaweed$planting_date <- as.Date(seaweed$planting_date)
se <- function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
summ <- seaweed %>% group_by(zone, technique) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(sgr, na.rm = TRUE), se = se(sgr), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(low = mean - 1.96 * se, high = mean + 1.96 * se)
summ                                                                  # 1
wq <- read.csv("data/checkpoints/I2_water_quality_clean.csv"); wq$date <- as.Date(wq$date)
st <- read.csv("data/stations.csv")
wq_zone <- wq %>% left_join(st[, c("station", "zone")], by = "station") %>%
  group_by(zone, date) %>% summarise(temp = mean(temp_C, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
wq_zone[which.max(wq_zone$temp), ]                                    # 2
sort(tapply(seaweed$sgr, seaweed$village, median, na.rm = TRUE))      # 3
seaweed %>% group_by(season, year) %>% summarise(m = round(mean(sgr, na.rm = TRUE), 3))  # 4
```
:::
